review_note: Filtered objects of abelian A form an additive category with zero, kernels/cokernels, images/coimages, but generally fail to be abelian. Matched against the pinned original theorem text in the Stage A source packet; did not open proof/remark text. Preliminary decision only.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
The category of filtered objects $\text{Fil}(\mathcal{A})$
has the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item It is an additive category.
\item It has a zero object.
\item It has kernels and cokernels, images and coimages.
\item In general it is not an abelian category.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category.
conclusions: $\mathrm{Fil}(\mathcal A)$ is additive with a zero object and kernels, cokernels, images and coimages.
In general, $\mathrm{Fil}(\mathcal A)$ is not abelian.

review_note: Strictness of a filtered-object morphism is characterized by the canonical coimage-to-image map being an isomorphism; the omitted lemma ref was correctly unpacked. Matched against the pinned original theorem text in the Stage A source packet; did not open proof/remark text. Preliminary decision only.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $f : A \to B$ be a morphism of filtered objects of $\mathcal{A}$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is strict,
\item the morphism $\Coim(f) \to \Im(f)$ (the canonical map factoring $f$ through its coimage and image)
is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: Let $f:A\to B$ be a morphism in $\mathrm{Fil}(\mathcal A)$ for an abelian $\mathcal A$.
conclusions: $f$ is strict iff the canonical comparison $\operatorname{Coim}(f)\to\operatorname{Im}(f)$ is an isomorphism in $\mathrm{Fil}(\mathcal A)$.

review_note: Adding any filtered morphism g to a strict mono f as the graph map A→B⊕C yields a strict monomorphism. Matched against the pinned original theorem text in the Stage A source packet; did not open proof/remark text. Preliminary decision only.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $f : A \to B$ be a strict monomorphism of filtered objects.
Let $g : A \to C$ be a morphism of filtered objects.
Then $f \oplus g : A \to B \oplus C$ is a strict monomorphism.
hypotheses: Let $f:A\to B$ be a strict monomorphism of filtered objects of an abelian category and $g:A\to C$ any filtered morphism.
conclusions: The map $(f,g):A\to B\oplus C$ is a strict monomorphism.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-add-summand-strict-monomorphism}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $f : A \to B$ be a strict monomorphism of filtered objects.
Let $g : A \to C$ be a morphism of filtered objects.
Then $f \oplus g : A \to B \oplus C$ is a strict monomorphism.

review_note: The sum morphism B⊕C→A is a strict epi when the first summand f already is a strict epi. Matched against the pinned original theorem text in the Stage A source packet; did not open proof/remark text. Preliminary decision only.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $f : B \to A$ be a strict epimorphism of filtered objects.
Let $g : C \to A$ be a morphism of filtered objects.
Then $f \oplus g : B \oplus C \to A$ is a strict epimorphism.
hypotheses: Let $f:B\to A$ be a strict epimorphism of filtered objects and $g:C\to A$ another filtered morphism.
conclusions: The map $(f,g):B\oplus C\to A$ is a strict epimorphism.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-add-summand-strict-epimorphism}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $f : B \to A$ be a strict epimorphism of filtered objects.
Let $g : C \to A$ be a morphism of filtered objects.
Then $f \oplus g : B \oplus C \to A$ is a strict epimorphism.

review_note: For injective filtered maps strictness means induced subobject filtration; for surjective ones it means quotient filtration. Matched against the pinned original theorem text in the Stage A source packet; did not open proof/remark text. Preliminary decision only.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $(A, F)$, $(B, F)$ be filtered objects.
Let $u : A \to B$ be a morphism of filtered objects.
If $u$ is injective then $u$ is strict if and only if the filtration
on $A$ is the induced filtration.
If $u$ is surjective then $u$ is strict if and only if the filtration
on $B$ is the quotient filtration.
hypotheses: Let $u:(A,F)\to(B,F)$ be a filtered morphism in an abelian category.
conclusions: If $u$ is monic, it is strict iff $F^pA=A\cap F^pB$ (via $u$) for all $p$.
If $u$ is epic, it is strict iff $F^pB=u(F^pA)$ for all $p$.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-induced-and-quotient-strict}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $(A, F)$, $(B, F)$ be filtered objects.
Let $u : A \to B$ be a morphism of filtered objects.
If $u$ is injective then $u$ is strict if and only if the filtration
on $A$ is the induced filtration.
If $u$ is surjective then $u$ is strict if and only if the filtration
on $B$ is the quotient filtration.

review_note: Composition of two strict filtered maps may fail strictness generally, but is strict when the second is mono or first is epi. Matched against the pinned original theorem text in the Stage A source packet; did not open proof/remark text. Preliminary decision only.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Let $f : A \to B$, $g : B \to C$
be strict morphisms of filtered objects.
\begin{enumerate}
\item In general the composition $g \circ f$ is not strict.
\item If $g$ is injective, then $g \circ f$ is strict.
\item If $f$ is surjective, then $g \circ f$ is strict.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: Let $f:A\to B$ and $g:B\to C$ be strict filtered morphisms.
conclusions: Their composite need not be strict.
It is strict if $g$ is monic.
It is strict if $f$ is epic.

review_note: The induced/quotient filtrations on Y/X agree and the six stated inclusions and quotient maps are strict. Matched against the pinned original theorem text in the Stage A source packet; did not open proof/remark text. Preliminary decision only.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $(A, F)$ be a filtered object of $\mathcal{A}$.
Let $X \subset Y \subset A$ be subobjects of $A$.
On the object
$$
Y/X = \Ker(A/X \to A/Y)
$$
the quotient filtration coming from the induced filtration on $Y$ and the
induced filtration coming from the quotient filtration on $A/X$ agree.
Any of the morphisms $X \to Y$, $X \to A$, $Y \to A$, $Y \to A/X$,
$Y \to Y/X$, $Y/X \to A/X$ are strict (with induced/quotient filtrations).
hypotheses: Let $X\subset Y\subset A$ be subobjects of a filtered object in an abelian category.
conclusions: The quotient and induced filtrations on $Y/X\cong\ker(A/X\to A/Y)$ coincide.
All six canonical inclusions/projections listed in the source are strict when equipped with the induced/quotient filtrations.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-filtration-subobject}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $(A, F)$ be a filtered object of $\mathcal{A}$.
Let $X \subset Y \subset A$ be subobjects of $A$.
On the object
$$
Y/X = \Ker(A/X \to A/Y)
$$
the quotient filtration coming from the induced filtration on $Y$ and the
induced filtration coming from the quotient filtration on $A/X$ agree.
Any of the morphisms $X \to Y$, $X \to A$, $Y \to A$, $Y \to A/X$,
$Y \to Y/X$, $Y/X \to A/X$ are strict (with induced/quotient filtrations).

review_note: Pushout exists among filtered objects and strictness of first input f is preserved along opposite pushout edge f′. Matched against the pinned original theorem text in the Stage A source packet; did not open proof/remark text. Preliminary decision only.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $A, B, C \in \text{Fil}(\mathcal{A})$.
Let $f : A \to B$ and $g : A \to C$ be morphisms.
Then there exists a pushout
$$
\xymatrix{
A \ar[r]_f \ar[d]_g & B \ar[d]^{g'} \\
C \ar[r]^{f'} & C \amalg_A B
}
$$
in $\text{Fil}(\mathcal{A})$. If $f$ is strict, so is $f'$.
hypotheses: Let $f:A\to B$ and $g:A\to C$ be morphisms in $\mathrm{Fil}(\mathcal A)$.
conclusions: The displayed pushout exists in $\mathrm{Fil}(\mathcal A)$; if $f$ is strict, the pushout map $f':C\to C\amalg_A B$ is strict.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-pushout-filtered}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $A, B, C \in \text{Fil}(\mathcal{A})$.
Let $f : A \to B$ and $g : A \to C$ be morphisms.
Then there exists a pushout
$$
\xymatrix{
A \ar[r]_f \ar[d]_g & B \ar[d]^{g'} \\
C \ar[r]^{f'} & C \amalg_A B
}
$$
in $\text{Fil}(\mathcal{A})$. If $f$ is strict, so is $f'$.

review_note: Filtered fibre product exists and pullback of strict f remains strict on induced f′ map. Matched against the pinned original theorem text in the Stage A source packet; did not open proof/remark text. Preliminary decision only.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $A, B, C \in \text{Fil}(\mathcal{A})$.
Let $f : B \to A$ and $g : C \to A$ be morphisms.
Then there exists a fibre product
$$
\xymatrix{
B \times_A C \ar[r]_{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} & B \ar[d]^f \\
C \ar[r]^g & A
}
$$
in $\text{Fil}(\mathcal{A})$. If $f$ is strict, so is $f'$.
hypotheses: Let $f:B\to A$ and $g:C\to A$ be morphisms in $\mathrm{Fil}(\mathcal A)$.
conclusions: Their pullback exists in $\mathrm{Fil}(\mathcal A)$; if $f$ is strict, the pullback map $f':B\times_A C\to C$ is strict.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-fibre-product-filtered}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $A, B, C \in \text{Fil}(\mathcal{A})$.
Let $f : B \to A$ and $g : C \to A$ be morphisms.
Then there exists a fibre product
$$
\xymatrix{
B \times_A C \ar[r]_{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} & B \ar[d]^f \\
C \ar[r]^g & A
}
$$
in $\text{Fil}(\mathcal{A})$. If $f$ is strict, so is $f'$.

review_note: Associated graded preserves exactness of an induced subobject/quotient filtered short exact sequence, and the kernel/coimage and image/cokernel sequences. Matched against the pinned original theorem text in the Stage A source packet; did not open proof/remark text. Preliminary decision only.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $A$ be a filtered object and $X \subset A$. Then for each $p$
the sequence
$$
0 \to \text{gr}^p(X) \to \text{gr}^p(A) \to \text{gr}^p(A/X) \to 0
$$
is exact (with induced filtration on $X$ and quotient filtration on $A/X$).
\item Let $f : A \to B$ be a morphism of filtered objects of $\mathcal{A}$.
Then for each $p$ the sequences
$$
0 \to \text{gr}^p(\Ker(f)) \to \text{gr}^p(A) \to
\text{gr}^p(\Coim(f)) \to 0
$$
and
$$
0 \to \text{gr}^p(\Im(f)) \to \text{gr}^p(B) \to
\text{gr}^p(\Coker(f)) \to 0
$$
are exact.
\end{enumerate}
conclusions: For $X\subset A$ filtered by induced filtration and $A/X$ by quotient filtration, the associated-graded sequence is short exact in every degree.
For a filtered map $f:A\to B$, both graded short exact sequences involving $\ker f$, $\operatorname{coim}f$, $\operatorname{im}f$, and $\operatorname{coker}f$ in the source are exact.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-ses-gr}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $A$ be a filtered object and $X \subset A$. Then for each $p$
the sequence
$$
0 \to \text{gr}^p(X) \to \text{gr}^p(A) \to \text{gr}^p(A/X) \to 0
$$
is exact (with induced filtration on $X$ and quotient filtration on $A/X$).
\item Let $f : A \to B$ be a morphism of filtered objects of $\mathcal{A}$.
Then for each $p$ the sequences
$$
0 \to \text{gr}^p(\Ker(f)) \to \text{gr}^p(A) \to
\text{gr}^p(\Coim(f)) \to 0
$$
and
$$
0 \to \text{gr}^p(\Im(f)) \to \text{gr}^p(B) \to
\text{gr}^p(\Coker(f)) \to 0
$$
are exact.
\end{enumerate}

review_note: Finite-filtration hypothesis is retained for the six-way strictness criteria, including exactness of associated-graded kernel/cokernel sequence. Matched against the pinned original theorem text in the Stage A source packet; did not open proof/remark text. Preliminary decision only.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $f : A \to B$ be a morphism of finite
filtered objects of $\mathcal{A}$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is strict,
\item the morphism $\Coim(f) \to \Im(f)$ is an isomorphism,
\item $\text{gr}(\Coim(f)) \to \text{gr}(\Im(f))$ is an
isomorphism,
\item the sequence
$\text{gr}(\Ker(f)) \to \text{gr}(A) \to \text{gr}(B)$
is exact,
\item the sequence $\text{gr}(A) \to \text{gr}(B) \to
\text{gr}(\Coker(f))$ is exact, and
\item the sequence
$$
0 \to
\text{gr}(\Ker(f)) \to
\text{gr}(A) \to
\text{gr}(B) \to
\text{gr}(\Coker(f)) \to 0
$$
is exact.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: Let $f:A\to B$ be a morphism of finite filtered objects of an abelian category.
conclusions: The six conditions listed in the source—strictness, the coimage/image isomorphism, its graded isomorphism, exactness at the middle of each of two graded sequences, and exactness of their combined five-term sequence—are equivalent.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-characterize-strict}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $f : A \to B$ be a morphism of finite
filtered objects of $\mathcal{A}$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is strict,
\item the morphism $\Coim(f) \to \Im(f)$ is an isomorphism,
\item $\text{gr}(\Coim(f)) \to \text{gr}(\Im(f))$ is an
isomorphism,
\item the sequence
$\text{gr}(\Ker(f)) \to \text{gr}(A) \to \text{gr}(B)$
is exact,
\item the sequence $\text{gr}(A) \to \text{gr}(B) \to
\text{gr}(\Coker(f))$ is exact, and
\item the sequence
$$
0 \to
\text{gr}(\Ker(f)) \to
\text{gr}(A) \to
\text{gr}(B) \to
\text{gr}(\Coker(f)) \to 0
$$
is exact.
\end{enumerate}

review_note: The source contains one unmatched right parenthesis; Stage A removes precisely that typo while preserving equality of associated graded homology for two strict complex maps. Matched against the pinned original theorem text in the Stage A source packet; did not open proof/remark text. Preliminary decision only.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Let $A \to B \to C$ be a complex
of filtered objects of $\mathcal{A}$. Assume $\alpha : A \to B$ and
$\beta : B \to C$ are strict morphisms of filtered objects. Then
$\text{gr}(\Ker(\beta)/\Im(\alpha)) =
\Ker(\text{gr}(\beta))/\Im(\text{gr}(\alpha))$.
hypotheses: Let $A\xrightarrow\alpha B\xrightarrow\beta C$ be a complex of filtered objects in an abelian category, and suppose $\alpha,\beta$ are strict.
conclusions: There is the source's equality $\operatorname{gr}(\ker\beta/\operatorname{im}\alpha)=\ker(\operatorname{gr}\beta)/\operatorname{im}(\operatorname{gr}\alpha)$.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-filtered-complex}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Let $A \to B \to C$ be a complex
of filtered objects of $\mathcal{A}$. Assume $\alpha : A \to B$ and
$\beta : B \to C$ are strict morphisms of filtered objects. Then
$\text{gr}(\Ker(\beta)/\Im(\alpha)) =
\Ker(\text{gr}(\beta))/\Im(\text{gr}(\alpha)))$.

review_note: Exactness on associated graded for finite filtered A→B→C implies each filtered level and quotient sequence exact and both maps strict. Matched against the pinned original theorem text in the Stage A source packet; did not open proof/remark text. Preliminary decision only.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $A \to B \to C$ be a complex of filtered objects of $\mathcal{A}$.
Assume $A, B, C$ have finite filtrations and that
$\text{gr}(A) \to \text{gr}(B) \to \text{gr}(C)$ is exact.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item for each $p \in \mathbf{Z}$ the sequence
$\text{gr}^p(A) \to \text{gr}^p(B) \to \text{gr}^p(C)$ is exact,
\item for each $p \in \mathbf{Z}$ the sequence
$F^p(A) \to F^p(B) \to F^p(C)$ is exact,
\item for each $p \in \mathbf{Z}$ the sequence
$A/F^p(A) \to B/F^p(B) \to C/F^p(C)$ is exact,
\item the maps $A \to B$ and $B \to C$ are strict, and
\item $A \to B \to C$ is exact (as a sequence in $\mathcal{A}$).
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: Let $A\to B\to C$ be a complex of finite filtered objects in an abelian category and suppose the associated graded complex is exact.
conclusions: Each graded degree sequence is exact.
Each filtration-level sequence is exact.
Each corresponding quotient filtration sequence is exact.
Both maps are strict.
The underlying unfiltered sequence is exact.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-filtered-acyclic}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $A \to B \to C$ be a complex of filtered objects of $\mathcal{A}$.
Assume $A, B, C$ have finite filtrations and that
$\text{gr}(A) \to \text{gr}(B) \to \text{gr}(C)$ is exact.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item for each $p \in \mathbf{Z}$ the sequence
$\text{gr}^p(A) \to \text{gr}^p(B) \to \text{gr}^p(C)$ is exact,
\item for each $p \in \mathbf{Z}$ the sequence
$F^p(A) \to F^p(B) \to F^p(C)$ is exact,
\item for each $p \in \mathbf{Z}$ the sequence
$A/F^p(A) \to B/F^p(B) \to C/F^p(C)$ is exact,
\item the maps $A \to B$ and $B \to C$ are strict, and
\item $A \to B \to C$ is exact (as a sequence in $\mathcal{A}$).
\end{enumerate}
